objective: Prove that inserting one ring into the twist tube's torus, a local rewiring of three contacts, turns <(2,1),(N,0)> into <(2,1),(N+1,0)>, so the law grows a network that keeps every contact persistent and reads its distance plainly at every stage from four rings; likewise for the triangular tube of a vector of length sqrt 3 and, by rungs, the ladder; and that every sequence of tori reading distance plainly at every stage is eventually a tube, so its balls grow linearly: such growth makes a line, not a plane.
status: Proved 2026-11-09: inserting one ring into the twist torus <(2,1),(N,0)>, a local rewiring of the three contacts spanning the gap, gives <(2,1),(N+1,0)>, so single-ring growth from 4 rings keeps every contact persistent and the plain first need on time at every stage (likewise the sqrt 3 triangular torus and the ladder by rungs); and every sequence of on-time tori of unbounded index is eventually a tube with balls of at most 4r + 1 rings, so such growth through tori grows a line, not a plane.
title: A single fastest way grows one ring at a time, and only along a line
